commits.message:
Markdown reads a line short of its container as indented less than any block, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.emsm) (#449)

* Markdown reads a line lazy to a quote's container as indented less than any block, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.emsm)

markdown-it gives a quote's lazy line sCount -1, and a list item's lazy line
sits short of the item's indentation, so a quote inside either checks its
terminators on that line as indented less than four. "> > b\n    ---" is the
quote "b", then indented code at the top level, in Rich 15; it was "b ---"
here. Same for a fence, an HTML block, a heading and a list item.

markdown-it's quote also takes a `>` line after its first at any indentation
("> a\n    > b" is one quote, "a b"), which the same function read as text.
Pinned against Rich 15 (markdown-it-py 4.2).

* Markdown indents a quote's line from its own `>`, wherever the `>` sits, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.emsm)

A list item's indent is now counted past each line's own margin, not as a
source column fixed by its first line, so a quote's `>` lines indented
differently from its first are read against the item as markdown-it reads them.

* Markdown reads a list item on a line lazy only to list items where the line sits, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.emsm)

A line lazy to a quote is indented less than any block; one lazy only to list
items keeps its indentation, and markdown-it's list refuses an item on it a
code indent past the list's container. Line.lazy now says which.

* Markdown reads a line short of a list item as indented less than any block, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.emsm, rich-unfiled-791c.w3t9)

An item's paragraph now reads the line it would take lazily the way a quote
does, and a lazy line carries the margin of the innermost list's container,
markdown-it's listIndent, which a list item on it is measured from.
